protective-award.title: FLX-06 · Protective-award scope
protective-award.scope: Inspect the recorded 90-to-180-day finding. Distinguish a tribunal award period from the Insolvency Service payment cap. No new legal rule is drafted in this batch.
protective-award.evidence_note: Current captured official guidance already states 180 days; the companion page describes a separate payment limit. This pack supports a no-edit decision from official guidance, not an independently traced statutory rule.
blockers: Any proposed change to the award or payment limits needs a separate traced legal-source pack.

scenarios.expected: Do not reintroduce an obsolete 90-day maximum.
Do not substitute 180 days for the separate combined eight-week payment cap.

paternity-scope.title: FFR-03 · Agency-worker scope check
paternity-scope.scope: Distinguish paternity-leave entitlement from the agency equal-treatment qualifying period. This page is not an eligibility decision for leave or pay.
paternity-scope.evidence_note: The captured agency page describes the 12-week equal-treatment clock and how absences affect it. The paternity pages keep leave and pay conditions separate.
blockers: Do not infer an agency worker’s leave or pay eligibility from this no-edit decision.

scenarios.expected: Keep the equal-treatment clock instructions.

scenarios.situation: Worker may qualify for pay but not leave
scenarios.expected: Do not infer identical eligibility from the two entitlements.

spl-order.title: Paternity / SPL · Order of leave
spl-order.scope: A coordinated edit to existing GOV.UK pages about the order of Paternity Leave and Shared Parental Leave. Retain all other eligibility, pay, curtailment, notice and timing conditions. Draft as current on 13 November 2026, not as an advance announcement.
spl-order.evidence_note: Section 17 removes the order restriction. SI 2026/3 regulation 4(4) commences the change on 6 April 2026, subject to Schedule 1: saved birth/adoption/overseas-adoption/parental-order cohorts, the early-birth exception and primary-carer-death exception. The broad current GOV.UK sentence does not spell out those boundaries.
blockers: Policy review required: confirm the plain-language rendering of all Schedule 1 cohorts, particularly parental-order cases and the statutory meaning of primary carer.
This does not determine entitlement to SPL, Paternity Leave or either statutory pay. Their conditions and operational regulations are outside this edit.
Coordinate worker and employer pages and the linked paternity guide; do not approve just one side of the journey.

scenarios.situation: Birth on 6 April 2026; eligible for both types of leave
scenarios.expected: Order restriction removed; ordinary eligibility, notice and timing requirements still apply.

scenarios.situation: Birth before 6 April; expected week begins 5 April 2026
scenarios.expected: Early-birth exception: the earlier restriction does not apply.

scenarios.situation: Birth before 6 April; expected week also before 5 April
scenarios.expected: Earlier restriction remains unless the primary-carer-death exception applies.
Earlier restriction remains unless the death exception applies.

scenarios.situation: Overseas adoption; entry to Great Britain before 6 April
scenarios.expected: Use entry date, not birth date or matching date.

scenarios.situation: Parental-order case; child born before 6 April
scenarios.expected: Use the parental-order cohort rule; do not apply the ordinary-birth expected-week exception.

scenarios.situation: Primary carer dies on or after 6 April
scenarios.expected: Schedule 1 paragraphs 1 and 2 do not apply; eligibility is not otherwise established.

scenarios.situation: Not eligible for SPL, or pay eligibility differs
scenarios.expected: Do not turn the removal of an order restriction into entitlement to leave or pay.
Do not extend the Great Britain change to this jurisdiction.
